chunks: "That is the place of the tent of the hypocrites, who, when they saw him raising his hand, some of them said to one another: 'Look at his eyes, turning as though they were the eyes of a madman.'

Then Jibril عليه السلام descended with this verse: "And those who disbelieve almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Remembrance, and they say: 'Indeed, he is surely mad.' And it is nothing but a reminder for the worlds."

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام informed Ḥassān al-Jammāl of that when he carried him from al-Madīnah to Makkah, and he said to him: "O Ḥassān, were it not that you are my camel-driver, I would not have narrated this hadith to you."

key_terms.الذِّكْرَ: the Reminder, referring here to the divine revelation
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الْآيَةِ: the Qur'anic verse revealed in response to the incident
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقِينَ: the hypocrites, those who concealed disbelief while outwardly professing faith
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibril عليه السلام, the angel who brought revelation
key_terms.فُسْطَاطِ: tent or encampment, referring here to the place associated with the hypocrites
key_terms.لَمَجْنُونٌ: surely mad, the false accusation made by the disbelievers
key_terms.لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ: they would almost cause you to slip or fall by their hostile looks

ai.seo_question: What is the context of the verse "And those who disbelieve almost make you slip with their eyes"?
ai.summary: This report explains that the verse was revealed concerning the hostile gaze and mockery of the disbelievers and hypocrites toward the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It presents the verse as a response to their accusation of madness and affirms that the Qur'an is only a reminder for all worlds.
